newsitem.title: INDIA: New crop arrival drag down Indian cotton prices.
newsitem.headline: New crop arrival drag down Indian cotton prices.

text.p: New arrivals and low mill demand dragged down Indian cotton prices on Tuesday, dealers said.
"Sentiment was also affected due to the absence of an anticipated announcement by the Indian government allowing more cotton export," one trader said.

New crop arrivals in the Punjab region rose on Tuesday to 30-35,000 bales (170 kg each) against the daily average of 20-25,000 bales last week. In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned slid by 5/10 rupees to 1,470/1,610 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell by five to 835/865. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) fell by 500 to 17,000/18,000 rupees.
